statement: The softmax function (also known as softargmax or normalized exponential function) converts a tuple of $K$ real numbers $\mathbf{z} = (z_1, \dots, z_K) \in \mathbb{R}^K$ into a probability distribution over $K$ possible outcomes, defined component-wise by $\sigma(\mathbf{z})_i = \frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_{k=1}^K e^{z_k}}$ for $i = 1, \dots, K$, or with an inverse temperature scaling factor $\beta$ (temperature $T = 1/\beta$) as $\sigma(\mathbf{z})_i = \frac{e^{\beta z_i}}{\sum_{j=1}^K e^{\beta z_j}}$.

symbols.meaning: input tuple or vector of real numbers (scores, state energies, or logits)
the i-th input real value or state energy
number of possible outcomes, classes, or microstates
output vector representing the normalized probability distribution
predicted probability of outcome or class i
scaling factor, inverse temperature, coldness, or thermodynamic beta

properties.property: Translation invariance: \sigma(\mathbf{z} + \mathbf{c}) = \sigma(\mathbf{z}) for constant vector \mathbf{c} = (c, \dots, c)
properties.why: Adding c to each coordinate multiplies every exponential term in the numerator and denominator by e^c, leaving the output ratio unchanged

properties.property: Maps \mathbb{R}^K to the open standard (K-1)-simplex where all components are positive and sum to 1
properties.why: Exponential terms are strictly positive and the denominator normalizes the components such that \sum_{i=1}^K \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i = 1

properties.property: Gradient of the LogSumExp function: \frac{\partial}{\partial z_i} \operatorname{LSE}(\mathbf{z}) = \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i
properties.why: Differentiating \operatorname{LSE}(\mathbf{z}) = \log(\sum_{k=1}^K \exp(z_k)) with respect to z_i yields \frac{\exp(z_i)}{\sum_{k=1}^K \exp(z_k)}

properties.property: Jacobian derivative: \frac{\partial}{\partial z_j} \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i = \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i (\delta_{ij} - \sigma(\mathbf{z})_j) (scaled by \beta if a scaling parameter is present)
properties.why: Differentiating the quotient of exponentials with respect to an input coordinate yields the product of \sigma_i and (\delta_{ij} - \sigma_j)

properties.property: Uniform distribution along the diagonal: \sigma(x, x, \dots, x) = (1/K, \dots, 1/K)
properties.why: Identical input scores produce equal exponential values that divide evenly across all K outcomes

properties.property: Argmax limit: as \beta \to \infty (temperature T \to 0), output concentrates on the arg max coordinate
properties.why: Differences between the maximum score and other scores become arbitrarily large relative to temperature, driving non-maximal probabilities to zero

assumptions.assumption: The input tuple components z_i are finite real numbers
assumptions.breaks_when: Any component z_i is infinite or NaN, making exponentiation undefined or non-finite

assumptions.assumption: The number of possible outcomes K is a finite positive integer (K \ge 1)
assumptions.breaks_when: K = 0, which leaves the denominator summation empty

assumptions.assumption: Temperature parameter T > 0 (or inverse temperature \beta is finite)
assumptions.breaks_when: Temperature T = 0, causing division by zero in exponent scaling

failure_modes.mode: Numerical overflow due to large exponentiation
failure_modes.signature: Intermediate values overflow to infinity, yielding inf / inf = NaN
failure_modes.cause: Large positive values in the input vector z cause e^{z_i} to exceed floating-point maximum limits before normalization; mitigated by safe softmax subtracting m = \max_i z_i

failure_modes.mode: Computational and memory bandwidth bottleneck at scale
failure_modes.signature: Excessive execution time and memory bandwidth saturation during forward and backward passes
failure_modes.cause: Computing the denominator normalization sum requires O(K) operations per sample, which becomes a bottleneck when K is very large (such as large language model vocabularies)
